one_liner: Flex-style C++ lexer generator plus a multi-engine regex matcher library; DFA scanners far outrun std::regex, PCRE2, and Boost.Regex at tokenizing.
what_it_does: RE/flex is a Flex-compatible lexical-analyzer generator: the `reflex` command compiles a .l lexer specification into a C++ DFA-based scanner (lex.yy.h/.cpp), and a companion library (libreflex) provides matcher classes (Matcher, PCRE2Matcher, BoostMatcher, StdMatcher, FuzzyMatcher) that share matches()/find()/scan()/split() methods and iterators over strings, wide strings, files, and streams. It targets tokenizing/scanning workloads, not one-off pattern checks, and it is not a drop-in replacement for std::regex/std::smatch call sites.
how_it_is_fast: The native RE/flex regex engine compiles patterns to a DFA using a backtrack-free lazy-matching transformation (credited to Robert van Engelen) that matches in linear time without backtracking, unlike std::regex's NFA engine. Generated scanners run as compact FSM code rather than re-entering a general matching engine per token. Matcher::find() and related search paths additionally use runtime-dispatched SIMD (SSE2/AVX2/AVX512BW on x86, NEON/AArch64 on Arm) to accelerate scanning for the next candidate match.
when_to_use: Tokenizing/scanning a stream into many tokens (lexer/parser front-ends) where std::regex's per-call setup and backtracking overhead dominate
Building a Flex/Bison-based C++ toolchain and wanting Unicode-aware, POSIX-compliant scanning with less porting effort than plain Flex++
Need indent/dedent-sensitive tokenizing (Python-like languages) or multi-encoding (UTF-8/16/32, legacy code pages) file input
Want one API that can fall back to PCRE2 or Boost.Regex for fuller Perl syntax while keeping the fast DFA engine on the hot path
Large text/file scanning workloads (RE/flex backs ugrep) where guaranteed linear-time DFA matching is preferable to std::regex's backtracking risk
when_not_to_use: Need capture groups with RE/flex's own fast engine: not supported natively (open issue #95, only non-capturing groups); must switch to PCRE2Matcher/BoostMatcher/StdMatcher and give up some speed
Need backreferences or lookaround: the native engine is IEEE POSIX P1003.2-compliant DFA matching, which structurally excludes these (only the PCRE2/Boost adapters support them)
Only need a handful of ad hoc regex checks in otherwise std::regex-shaped code: the reflex code-generation step plus a libreflex build add more integration surface than warranted

Pattern shapes with a leading unanchored wildcard (e.g. `.*literal`) used with Matcher::find(): one reported benchmark (#220) showed ~15000x slowdown versus removing the leading `.*`, so verify your actual pattern shape
Strict correctness under MemorySanitizer: issue #234 reports a use-of-uninitialized-value warning in AbstractMatcher::reset_text() via text()

integration.dependencies: none required; PCRE2 and Boost.Regex are optional, only needed if you use reflex::PCRE2Matcher or reflex::BoostMatcher
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 11 in CMakeLists.txt); strview() needs C++17
integration.platforms: Windows, macOS, Linux, NetBSD, BSD; x86-64 with SSE2/AVX2/AVX512BW auto-detected at runtime (configure --disable-avx / --disable-sse2 to turn off), aarch64/NEON supported for search, portable C++ fallback otherwise
integration.thread_safety: not documented as a formal guarantee; README states multiple generated lexer classes can be used by multiple threads, implying each thread should own its own matcher/lexer instance rather than share one
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: reflex::StdMatcher wraps std::regex behind RE/flex's own API (not source-compatible with std::regex/std::smatch code), and the fast native engine additionally requires a build-time code-generation step (the reflex tool), so no matcher class is a header-swap drop-in for std::regex

gotchas: Native Matcher has no capture groups (non-capturing groups only); this is a known, still-open design gap, not a bug that will be fixed soon
A leading unanchored `.*` in a pattern used with find() can be ~15000x slower than the equivalent anchored/literal search on the same input (issue #220)
libreflex is a real build artifact (libreflex.a/.so via configure/make or CMake), not a header you can just #include and go
SIMD (AVX2/AVX512BW) is auto-detected at runtime by default; disable via configure flags if you hit CPU-detection or build issues on older toolchains
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick RE/flex over Boost.Regex, REAL, or Unformat when the job is generating a real tokenizer/scanner (many tokens per input, Flex/Bison-style workflow) rather than replacing scattered std::regex match/search calls; Boost.Regex and REAL are closer to a source-level drop-in for individual std::regex call sites with far less build/integration surface.
verified_claims_summary: On a 2 KB representative C source file tokenized into 244 tokens, a reflex --fast --noindent generated scanner (RE/flex 3.4.1) measured 8.7 us versus 6490 us for std::cregex_iterator (C++11 std::regex, libc++ inferred from platform) — about 746x faster — measured with clang 12.0.0 -O2 on a 2.9 GHz Intel Core i7 / 16 GB LPDDR3 Mac running macOS 12.6.9. The repo is now at 6.5.0; the std::regex leg was run through RE/flex's own std-ecma matcher adapter with one large alternation pattern rather than a hand-written std::regex loop.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-15, now versioned 6.5.0 vs. the benchmarked 3.4.1) and BSD-3-Clause/copyable, but the reflex code-generation step and libreflex build make it heavier to vendor than a header-only std::regex replacement.
